# Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/2024 of 26 July 2024 supplementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1056 by establishing the eFTI common data set and eFTI data subsets

**COMMISSION DELEGATED REGULATION (EU) 2024/2024**

**of 26 July 2024**

**supplementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1056 by establishing the eFTI common data set and eFTI data subsets**

**(Text with EEA relevance)**

THE EUROPEAN COMMISSION,

Having regard to the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union,

Having regard to Regulation (EU) 2020/1056 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 15 July 2020 on electronic freight transport information (1), and in particular Article 7 thereof,

Whereas:

(1) Regulation (EU) 2020/1056 should be supplemented to establish the eFTI common data set and the eFTI data subsets.

(2) Article 3(5) of Regulation (EU) 2020/1056 specifies that each eFTI data subset should comprise the structured set of data elements corresponding to the regulatory information required in a specific Union legal act or national law. Article 3(6) of the same Regulation specifies that the eFTI common data set should comprise the comprehensive set of structured data elements that correspond to all the eFTI data subsets, where the data elements common to the different eFTI data subsets are included only once. Furthermore, Article 3(7) specifies that each eFTI data element should have a unique definition and precise technical characteristics, such as format, length and character type.

(3) The purpose of establishing the eFTI common data set is to simplify data recording and exchange in an electronic format, and thus ensure the availability of consistent information, for the purposes of checking and proving compliance with transport rules. Standardised names, definitions and formats of the data elements common across the different eFTI subsets including, where applicable, harmonised code lists and business rules, will allow economic operators to record data in a clear and standardised format. Furthermore, a harmonised structure for these data elements will enable this data to be exchanged automatically between the operators’ eFTI platforms and the IT systems of the competent authorities.

(4) The freight transport information to be recorded and exchanged within the eFTI environment is, for the most part, the same information that economic operators need to exchange in the business domain in order to ensure operational flows, as well as to prove their compliance with other regulatory requirements outside the scope of Regulation (EU) 2020/1056. To allow the reuse of eFTI data for such other exchanges, and ensure interoperability with relevant business-to-business and business-to-authorities electronic exchange environments, it is important to align the structure and definition of the data elements comprised in the eFTI common data set and eFTI data subsets with those of the corresponding data elements in the three most relevant Union and international data models: the Union Customs Code data model (EU CDM) (2), the European Maritime Single Window environment (EMSWe) data model (3), and the UN/CEFACT Multi Modal Transport Reference Data Model (MMT-RDM) (4). This will enable more efficient sharing and reuse of data, reduce the administrative burden for economic operators and improve the quality of the freight information the authorities can access to check compliance with applicable rules.

(5) Article 83(4) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1157 of the European Parliament and of the Council (5) amends Article 7 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1056, to set a later date for the adoption of the specifications of the eFTI data subset corresponding to the information requirements related to the movement of waste falling under the scope of Regulation (EU) 2020/1056, as referred to in point (iv) of Article 2(1)(a) of that regulation. Therefore, those specifications should not be adopted by this delegated regulation. To allow alignment with the related specifications to be adopted under the implementing regulations referred to in Article 27(5) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1157, those specifications should be adopted at a later stage and no later than the date referred to in that article.

(6) The Commission has carried out appropriate consultations, including at expert level and with stakeholders (6),

HAS ADOPTED THIS REGULATION:

## Article 1 — Establishment of the eFTI common data set and of the eFTI data subsets

The eFTI common data set and the eFTI data subsets provided for under Article 7 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1056 are set out in the Annex to this Regulation.

## Article 2 — Entry into force and application

This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.

It shall apply from the date of entry into force of this Regulation.

This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.

Done at Brussels, 26 July 2024.

For the Commission

The President

Ursula VON DER LEYEN

(1) OJ L 249, 31.7.2020, p. 33.

(2) As established under Regulation (EU) No 952/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 9 October 2013 laying down the Union Customs Code (OJ L 269, 10.10.2013, p. 1).

(3) As established under Regulation (EU) 2019/1239 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20 June 2019 establishing a European Maritime Single Window environment and repealing Directive 2010/65/EU (OJ L 198, 25.7.2019, p. 64).

(4) https://unece.org/trade/uncefact/rdm.

(5) Regulation (EU) 2024/1157 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 April 2024 on shipments of waste, amending Regulations (EU) No 1257/2013 and (EU) 2020/1056 and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006 (OJ L, 2024/1157, 30.4.2024, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1157/oj).

(6) Documents and reports of the relevant meetings can be found on the Register of Commission expert groups and other similar entities (europa.eu). Stakeholder feedback received on the draft act shared on the Commission ‘Have your say’ portal can be found here.

## ANNEX — eFTI COMMON DATA SET AND eFTI DATA SUBSETS

**SECTION 1**

**Introductory notes**

|  | A. | As per the definitions provided in points (5), (6) and (7) of Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1056, the eFTI common data set and eFTI data subsets are not just lists of data elements, but ‘set[s] of structured data elements’, where all the data elements corresponding to all of the subsets constitute the common data set, with the data elements common to two or more subsets included only once. Those definitions also indicate that each data element should be described through specific properties such as definition and technical characteristics, including format, length and character type, and that what distinguishes a data element in the common data set is their ‘unique definition’. Several data elements may share therefore one or more properties such as format or character type, but not the definition. |

**SECTION 2**

**eFTI common data set**

<table>
<tbody><tr><td></td><td>A.</td><td>The eFTI common data set is described in Table 1, where:<table><tbody><tr><td>1.</td><td>Column with heading ‘H*’ represents the structure of the common data set by indicating the hierarchy level of the data objects, either data classes or data elements. This hierarchical structure begins with level 1. Each data object directly subordinated to level 1 is marked with level 2, each data object directly subordinated to level 2 is marked with level 3 and so on and so forth. Each data object is a subordinated component of the last preceding object in the table at higher level. Example:  Data element eFTI41 ‘Gross mass’ is marked with hierarchy level 3. It is subordinated to the last preceding data object at higher level, i.e. level 2, which is data class ASBIE1027 ‘eFTI data set consignment’. The subordinated component of data element eFTI41 is data element eFTI42 ‘Measurement unit code’, which is marked with level 4. </td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>2.</td><td>Column with heading ‘Object Type’ indicates:<table><tbody><tr><td>(a)</td><td>data classes, when the reference provided is ‘ASBIE’. Data classes are groupings of data elements describing a certain piece of information;</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(b)</td><td>data elements, when the reference provided is ‘BBIE’ or ‘SC’. Data elements marked as ‘SC’ are always related to a ‘BBIE’ data element, as they constitute supplementary units of information necessary to fully specify the information provided by the BBIE data element (2);</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(c)</td><td>the comprehensive hierarchical structure of the eFTI common data set, by means of the graphical lines on the left side of the column.</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>3.</td><td>Column with heading ‘ID’ indicates the data element identification number in format ‘eFTIxxx(x)’, which uniquely identifies the data element in the eFTI common data set. The identification number is automatically assigned and indicates neither sequence nor hierarchy of the data element in the eFTI common data set.</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>4.</td><td>Column with heading ‘L*’ indicates, when provided, the data elements that will be accompanied by a language indicator providing information on the language of the content of the data field.</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>5.</td><td>Column with heading ‘Name and Definition’ indicates, in separate rows:<table><tbody><tr><td>(a)</td><td>the standard, non-technical name of the data element;</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(b)</td><td>the short textual description of the data element;</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(c)</td><td>when provided, the reference of specific rules (in format ‘BR-xxx’) that need to be applied in relation to the use of a data element when certain conditions are met. These rules are detailed in Section 6.</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>6.</td><td>Column with heading ‘Data Type’ indicates what kind of value the data element can hold. Example: ‘quantity’ indicates that the data element can hold a number expressing the count of non-monetary units. </td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>7.</td><td>Column with heading ‘Format’ indicates the requirements for the data type and the data length, where:<table><tbody><tr><td>(a)</td><td>the codes for the data types are as follows:<table><tbody><tr><td>(i)</td><td>‘a’ means alphabetic;</td></tr>

</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(ii)</td><td>‘n’ means numeric;</td></tr>

</table>
</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(b)</td><td>the number following the code indicates the admissible data length, where:<table><tbody><tr><td>(i)</td><td>the optional two dots before the length indicator mean that the data has no fixed length, but it can have up to a number of digits, as specified by the length indicator;</td></tr>

<table><tbody><tr><td>(ii)</td><td>a comma in the data length means that the attribute can hold decimals, where the digit before the comma indicates the total length of the attribute and the digit after the comma indicates the maximum number of digits after the decimal point. **SECTION 3**

**eFTI data subsets corresponding to information requirements in EU legal acts provisions**

<table>
<tbody><tr><td></td><td>A.</td><td>The data subsets corresponding to information requirements in EU legal acts provisions, as referred in Article 2(1) of Regulation (EU) 2020/1056, are described in Table 2, where:<table><tbody><tr><td>1.</td><td>The numbering of the data subsets follows the sequence of the EU legal provisions listed in Article 2(1)(a) of Regulation (EU) 2020/1056. To identify these subsets, the following references are used:<table><tbody><tr><td>(a)</td><td>‘EU01’ indicates the eFTI subset consisting of the data elements that correspond to the information requirements set out in Article 6(1) of EEC Council Regulation No 11, as referred to in point (i) of Article 2(1)(a) of Regulation (EU) 2020/1056;</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(b)</td><td>‘EU02’ indicates the eFTI subset consisting of the data elements that correspond to the information requirements set out in Article 3 of Council Directive 92/106/EEC, as referred to in point (ii) of Article 2(1)(a) of Regulation (EU) 2020/1056;</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(c)</td><td>‘EU03’ indicates the eFTI subset consisting of the data elements that correspond to the information requirements set out in Article 8(3) of Regulation (EC) No 1072/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council, as referred to in point (iii) of Article 2(1)(a) of Regulation (EU) 2020/1056;</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(d)</td><td>‘EU05a’ indicates the eFTI subset consisting of the data elements that correspond to the information requirements set out the in the provisions of the international agreements on the transport of dangerous goods referred to in Section I.1 of Annex I to Directive 2008/68/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council, as referred to in point (v) of Article 2(1)(a) of Regulation (EU) 2020/1056;</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(e)</td><td>‘EU05b’ indicates the eFTI subset consisting of the data elements that correspond to the information requirements set out the in the provisions of the international agreements on the transport of dangerous goods referred to in Section II.1 of Annex II to Directive 2008/68/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council, as referred to in point (v) of Article 2(1)(a) of Regulation (EU) 2020/1056;</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(f)</td><td>‘EU05c’ indicates the eFTI subset consisting of the data elements that correspond to the information requirements set out the in the provisions of the international agreements on the transport of dangerous goods referred to in Section III.1 of Annex III to Directive 2008/68/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council, as referred to in point (v) of Article 2(1)(a) of Regulation (EU) 2020/1056;</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(g)</td><td>‘EU06’ indicates the eFTI subset consisting of the data elements that correspond to the information requirements set out in Annex 6.3.2.6 (a), (b), (c), (d), (e), (f) and (g) of Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1998 (3), as referred to in point (1) of Part A of Annex I to Regulation (EU) 2020/1056.</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>2.</td><td>Column with heading ‘H*’ represents the structure of the data subset by indicating the hierarchy level of the data objects, either data classes or data elements. This hierarchical structure begins with level 0. Each data object directly subordinated to level 0 is marked with level 1, each data object directly subordinated to level 1 is marked with level 2 and so on and so forth. Each data object is a subordinated component of the last preceding object in the table at higher level. Example:  Data element eFTI41 is marked with hierarchy level 2. It is subordinated to the last preceding data object at higher level, i.e. level 1, which is data class ASBIE1027. The subordinated component of data element eFTI41 is data element eFTI42, which is marked with level 3. </td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>3.</td><td>Column with heading ‘Object Type’ indicates:<table><tbody><tr><td>(a)</td><td>data classes, when the reference provided is ‘ASBIE’. Data classes are groupings of data elements describing a certain piece of information;</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(b)</td><td>data elements, when the reference provided is ‘BBIE’ or ‘SC’. Data elements marked as ‘SC’ are always related to a ‘BBIE’ data element, as they constitute supplementary units of information necessary to fully specify the information provided by the BBIE data element (4).</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>4.</td><td>Column with heading ‘ID’ indicates the identification number of the data element as assigned in the eFTI common data set (‘eFTIxxx(x)’).</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>5.</td><td>The header of a group of 3 columns, in format ‘EUyy’, indicates the unique identification number of the data subset, where ‘EU’ stands for the European Union and ‘yy’ stands for the number of the subset. Each of the 3 columns under this header provides details about this specific subset.</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>6.</td><td>Column with heading ‘LS’ indicates the legal status of the data element in the context of the specific subset, where:<table><tbody><tr><td>(a)</td><td>status ‘M’ indicates that the Economic Operator must provide this information;</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(b)</td><td>status ‘C’ indicates that providing this information is conditional, depending on the provision of some other information;</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(c)</td><td>status ‘O’ indicates that providing this information is optional;</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(d)</td><td>status ‘D*’ indicates that this is a supplementary unit of information that is necessary to be provided to fully specify the information provided for the data element to which it is related;</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(e)</td><td>status ‘SI’ indicates that this is a data class and not a data element, where ‘SI’ stands for ‘structural indicator’.</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>7.</td><td>Column with heading ‘BR(s)’ indicates, when provided, the reference of specific rules (in format ‘BR-xxx’) that need to be applied in relation to the use of a data element when certain conditions are met in the context of this specific subset. The aim of these rules is to ensure that the value to be provided for the respective data element corresponds to the specific conditions laid down in the corresponding regulatory information requirement, including how that value would relate to the value of other data elements necessary to express the respective required information. These rules are detailed in Section 6.</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>8.</td><td>Column with heading ‘Code(s)’ indicates, when provided, a selection of codes that are allowed to be used in the context of this specific subset from the applied code list. In case no subset-specific code restrictions are mentioned, the same restrictions apply to the data element as in the context of the eFTI common data set (Table 1, column ‘Allowed Codes’).</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

**SECTION 4**

**eFTI data subsets corresponding to information requirements in provisions of national law**

<table>
<tbody><tr><td></td><td>A.</td><td>The eFTI data subsets corresponding to information requirements in provisions of national law, as listed in the Annex to Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/2025, are described in Tables 3 to 29, where:<table><tbody><tr><td>1.</td><td>To identify the subsets, references in format ‘XXyy’ are used, where ‘XX’ stands for the two-letter country code for each Member State (e.g. AT, BE, BG etc.) and ‘yy’ stands for the number of the subset. The subsets’ numbering follows the sequence in which the respective national provisions are listed in the Annex to Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/2025.</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>2.</td><td>Column with heading ‘H*’ represents the structure of the data subset by indicating the hierarchy level of the data objects, either data classes or data elements. This hierarchical structure begins with level 0. Each data object directly subordinated to level 0 is marked with level 1, each data object directly subordinated to level 1 is marked with level 2 and so on and so forth. Each data object is a subordinated component of the last preceding object in the table at higher level. Example:  Data element eFTI41 is marked with hierarchy level 2. It is subordinated to the last preceding data object at higher level, i.e. level 1, which is data class ASBIE1027. The subordinated component of data element eFTI41 is data element eFTI42 ‘Measurement unit code’, which is marked with level 3. </td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>3.</td><td>Column with heading ‘Object Type’ indicates:<table><tbody><tr><td>(a)</td><td>data classes, when the reference provided is ‘ASBIE’. Data classes are groupings of data elements describing a certain piece of information;</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(b)</td><td>data elements, when the reference provided is ‘BBIE’ or ‘SC’. Data elements marked as ‘SC’ are always related to a ‘BBIE’ data element, as they constitute supplementary units of information necessary to fully specify the information provided by the BBIE data element (5).</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>4.</td><td>Column with heading ‘ID’ indicates the identification number of the data element as assigned in the eFTI common data set (‘eFTIxxx(x)’).</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>5.</td><td>The header of a group of 3 columns, in format ‘XXyy’, indicates the unique identification number of the data subset, as described in point 1 above. Each of the 3 columns under that header provides details about this specific subset.</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>6.</td><td>Column with heading ‘LS’ indicates the legal status of the data element in the context of the specific subset, where:<table><tbody><tr><td>(a)</td><td>status ‘M’ indicates that the Economic Operator must provide this information;</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(b)</td><td>status ‘C’ indicates that providing this information is conditional, depending on the provision of some other information;</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(c)</td><td>status ‘O’ indicates that providing this information is optional;</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(d)</td><td>status ‘D*’ indicates that this is a supplementary unit of information that is necessary to be provided to fully specify the information provided for the data element to which it is related;</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(e)</td><td>status ‘SI’ indicates that this is a data class and not a data element, where ‘SI’ stands for ‘structural indicator’.</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>7.</td><td>Column with heading ‘BR(s)’ indicates, when provided, the reference of specific rules (in format ‘BR-xxx’) that need to be applied in relation to the use of a data element when certain conditions are met in the context of this specific subset. The aim of these rules is to ensure that the value to be provided for the respective data element corresponds to the specific conditions laid down in the corresponding regulatory information requirement, including how that value would relate to the value of other data elements necessary to express the respective required information. These rules are detailed in Section 6.</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>8.</td><td>Column with heading ‘Code(s)’ indicates, when provided, a selection of codes that are allowed to be used in the context of this specific subset from the applied code list. In case no subset-specific code restrictions are mentioned, the same restrictions apply to the data element as in the context of the eFTI common data set (Table 1, column ‘Allowed Codes’).</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

|  | B. |  |
| --- | --- | --- |

**SECTION 5**

**Code lists**

<table>
<tbody><tr><td></td><td>A.</td><td>Table 30 provides the name of the code list for each code list reference used in the eFTI common data set. It also provides the indication of all the codes that are allowed to be used from that specific code list at the level of the entire eFTI common data set, where:<table><tbody><tr><td>1.</td><td>Column with heading ‘eFTI Code list ID’ indicates a specific reference for each code list required by at least one data element; these code lists references have been established for the purposes of this Delegated Regulation and do not apply elsewhere;</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>2.</td><td>Column with heading ‘Code list name’ indicates the full name of the code list and includes in brackets a reference to either the legal provisions based on which the code list has been established (for example ADR/RID 1.1.3.6) or to the agency that maintains the code list (for example UNECE);</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>3.</td><td>Column with heading ‘Allowed codes’ indicates:<table><tbody><tr><td>(a)</td><td>if in the context of the eFTI common data set all codes of this code list are allowed to be used; or,</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(b)</td><td>when only a selection of codes from this code list are allowed to be used, all codes and their values of this code list that are used by at least one data element.</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<table>
<tbody><tr><td></td><td>B.</td><td>There are 3 different types of code lists:<table><tbody><tr><td>(a)</td><td>Code lists that have been specifically defined for usage in the context of the eFTI Regulation implementation, where the code definitions are available in legal acts (EU legal acts, national legal acts or international conventions). Example:  CL-006 (eFTI CSD screening method (Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1998 Annex 6.3.2.6 (e)(iv))). </td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(b)</td><td>Code lists that have been specifically defined for usage in the context of the eFTI Regulation implementation, including the code definitions. Example:  CL-010 (eFTI Container pick-up/drop-off). </td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<table><tbody><tr><td>(c)</td><td>Code lists published outside the EU legal framework, for example by international organisations such as the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) or the United Nations Centre for Trade Facilitation and Electronic Business (UN/CEFACT). For these code lists only a reference is given and an indication of which codes are allowed from that list. Example:  CL-017 (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (UNECE (UN/EDIFACT) codes 3207) All codes of this code list are allowed). </td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<tr><td>BR-090</td><td>eFTI307</td><td>For the carriage of cylinders, tubes, pressure drums, cryogenic receptacles and bundles of cylinders under the conditions of ADR/RID 4.1.6.10, the following entry shall be included in the transport document: ‘Carriage in accordance with 4.1.6.10’.</td></tr>

<tr><td>BR-093</td><td>eFTI374; eFTI448; eFIT618</td><td>If a transport means, equipment, packages are used for dangerous goods transport, and identification numbers are available, then an identification shall be provided.</td></tr>

<tr><td>BR-096</td><td>eFTI424; eFTI550</td><td>If empty tanks, battery-vehicles and MEGCs, uncleaned, are carried to the nearest place where cleaning or repair can be carried out in accordance with the provisions of ADR/RID 4.3.2.4.3, the following additional entry shall be made in the transport document: ‘Carriage in accordance with 4.3.2.4.3’.</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-097</td><td>eFTI424; eFTI550</td><td>If empty vehicles and containers, uncleaned, are carried to the nearest place where cleaning or repair can be carried out in accordance with the provisions of ADR/RID 7.5.8.1, the following additional entry shall be made in the transport document: ‘Carriage in accordance with 7.5.8.1’.</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-098</td><td>eFTI317</td><td>If the proper shipping name of a substance which is carried or offered for carriage in a liquid state at a temperature equal to or exceeding 100 °C, or in a solid state at a temperature equal to or exceeding 240 °C, does not convey the elevated temperature condition (for example, by using the term ‘MOLTEN’ or ‘ELEVATED TEMPERATURE’ as part of the proper shipping name), the word ‘HOT’ shall immediately precede the proper shipping name.</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-099</td><td>eFTI279; eFTI283 </td><td>If the word ‘STABILIZED’ is part of the proper shipping name and stabilization is done by means of temperature control.</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-100</td><td>eFTI317</td><td>In all cases of international carriage of packages requiring competent authority approval of design or shipment, for which different approval types apply in the different countries concerned by the shipment, the UN number and proper shipping name required in ADR/RID/ADN 5.4.1.1.1 shall be in accordance with the certificate of the country of origin of design.</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-101</td><td>eFTI238; eFTI243; eFTI247</td><td>It does not apply to carriage of packagings, discarded, empty, uncleaned (UN 3509).</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-102</td><td>eFTI825</td><td>Applies only in cases covered by ADN or ADR.</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-103</td><td>eFTI240</td><td>Mandatory for rail.</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-104</td><td>eFTI374</td><td>RID only, applies to trains carrying dangerous goods.</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-105</td><td>eFTI281; eFTI285</td><td>To be used in case of ADR/ADN 5.4.1.1.15 statement.</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-106</td><td>eFTI317</td><td>When a sample of an organic peroxide (see ADR/RID/ADN 2.2.52.1.9) or a self-reactive substance (see ADR/RID/ADN 2.2.41.1.15) is carried, a statement to this effect shall be included in the transport document, e.g. ‘Carriage in accordance with 2.2.52.1.9’.</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-107</td><td>eFTI317</td><td>When a substance, which is solid in accordance with the definition in ADR/RID/ADN 1.2.1, is offered for carriage in the molten state, the qualifying word ‘MOLTEN’ shall be added as part of the proper shipping name, unless it is already part of the proper shipping name (see 3.1.2.5).</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-108</td><td>eFTI346</td><td>When by derogation from ADR/ADN 5.3.2.1.2 a multi-compartment tank-vehicle or a transport unit with more than one tank is marked in accordance with ADR/ADN 5.3.2.1.3, the substances contained in each tank or in each compartment of a tank shall be specified in the transport document.</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-109</td><td>eFTI970</td><td>When explosive substances or articles are carried in packagings conforming to packing instruction P101, the transport document shall bear the inscription ‘Packaging approved by the competent authority of …’ (see ADR/RID 4.1.4.1, packing instruction P101).</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-110</td><td>eFTI319</td><td>When goods mentioned by name in Table A of ADR Chapter 3.2, are not subject to ADR because they are considered as non-dangerous according to Part 2, the consignor may enter in the transport document a statement to that effect, e.g.: ‘Not goods of Class …’.</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-111</td><td>eFTI320</td><td>Applies to the carriage of mixtures (see RID 2.2.2.1.1) in tank-wagons, battery-wagons, wagons with demountable tanks, portable tanks, tank-containers or MEGCs. It does not apply when the technical names authorized by special provisions 581, 582 or 583 are used to supplement the proper shipping name, or when the composition of the mixture as a percentage of the volume is given.</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-112</td><td>eFTI587; eFTI589</td><td>When place of loading (ASBIE1100) is different from the place of acceptance (ASBIE1048), one of the following should be provided: data element eFTI587, data element eFTI589 or an appropriate combination of data elements belonging to ASBIE1100 (Place of loading).</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-113</td><td>eFTI600; eFTI602</td><td>When place of unloading (ASBIE1104) is different from the place of delivery (ASBIE1051), one of the following should be provided: data element eFTI600, data element eFTI602 or an appropriate combination of data elements belonging to ASBIE1104 (Place of unloading).</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-114a</td><td>eFTI593; eFTI594;</td><td>When business rule BR-112 is applied, then this information must be provided.</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-114b</td><td>eFTI606; eFTI608</td><td>When business rule BR-113 is applied, then this information must be provided.</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-115</td><td>eFTI590; eFTI592</td><td>When a place of loading is provided (ASBIE1100), then at least name or identification number of the certifying (= stamping) station or port authority must be provided. This applies also to situations where the place of loading is identical with the place of acceptance.</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-116</td><td>eFTI603; eFTI605</td><td>When a place of unloading is provided (ASBIE1104), then at least name or identification number of the certifying (= stamping) station or port authority must be provided. This includes applies also to the situations where the place of unloading is identical with the place of delivery.</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-117</td><td>eFTI1137; eFTI1139 </td><td>If empty container drop-off is to be specified, then at least either identification number or place name must be specified.</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-118</td><td>eFTI1137; eFTI1139 </td><td>If empty container pick-up is to be specified, then at least either identification number or place name must be specified.</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-119</td><td>eFTI1135</td><td>Must be used if empty container drop-off is to be specified.</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-120</td><td>eFTI1135</td><td>Must be used if empty container pick-up is to be described.</td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-121</td><td>eFTI169</td><td>If the consignment information concerns only one House Air Waybill (AWB), then only one AWB number can be provided. If the consignment information concerns a Master AWB, then nil to many House AWB numbers can be provided. </td></tr>
<tr><td>BR-122</td><td>eFTI848</td><td>If AOM is used, then the method used shall be specified.</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
